newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst to merge specialty chemicals units.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst to merge specialty chemicals units.

text.p: Hoechst AG, Europe's largest chemicals group, said Tuesday it plans to merge its flagging speciality chemicals business with Swiss group Clariant AG into a new industry leader, but at a cost of heavy job losses.

Hoechst told German stock market authorities it would merge virtually all of its speciality chemicals business, including pigments and additives as well as other businesses, into a new group and take a minority stake of 40-45 percent in Clariant.

The new group, also called Clariant and expected to be the global industry leader, will post sales of 9 billion marks ($5.8 billion) in annual sales, Hoechst board member Karl-Gerhard Seifert told Reuters.

Acknowledging that Hoechst's speciality chemicals have been an underperformer plagued by restructurings for some time, Seifert said he hopes the new group will be a "very profitable European chemicals group."
For Hoechst the merger will improve the group's presence in Asia and the United States and improve the portfolio, Seifert said.
While each company stands to reap enormous savings estimated at around 600 million marks ($387 million), about 16 percent of all jobs will be lost.
"We expect to cut around 5,000 jobs worldwide over the next three years in a socially acceptable manner," reducing the work force from 31,000 at the moment, Seifert said.
Although no major plant closures are planned at the moment, Seiftert said he could not rule out such steps in the future as the group does not need to keep its 120 sites operating.
For Hoechst, having made no secret of its hopes to spin off the speciality chemicals business, the deal further underscores its efforts to focus more on life-sciences, Seifert added.

Hoechst, providing 6.5 billion marks ($4.2 billion) in sales to the new group, said Clariant will remain a Swiss company, quoted on the Zurich stock exchange. Clariant will bring 2.7 billion marks ($1.7 billion) in sales the new group.
Analysts welcomed the deal, saying Hoechst had taken a bold step in revamping a sector that some analysts believed had been mismanaged for some time.
Seifert shrugged off the fact that Switzerland, like Germany, is generally plagued by very high costs, saying that Clariant is an internationally diverse group, which helps bring down costs.
